jobs.title: Chief of Staff, Office of the CEO
jobs.description:
What is Coast

Coast is re-imagining the trillion-dollar U.S. B2B card payments infrastructure, with a focus on the country's 500,000 commercial fleets, 40 million commercial vehicles, and many millions of commercial drivers. The incumbent technologies that cater to these customers are decades old, and businesses with fleets increasingly demand modern digital experiences and transparent financial services products. Coast's mission is to deliver this at a transformational scale, beginning with the Coast Fleet and Fuel Card built on a cutting-edge spend management platform.

About the Role

The Chief of Staff is the CEO's most trusted operating partner. You will extend his reach across the company: representing him in rooms he cannot be in, carrying his priorities into the executive team, and making sure the decisions that matter get made, communicated, and executed. This is not a coordination or scheduling role. When you speak, the company should understand that you speak with the CEO's full context and backing.

You will sit at the center of the business. In a given month you might drive the leadership team's operating cadence, pressure-test an executive's plan on the CEO's behalf, prepare and help run a board meeting, own a company-critical special project end to end, or step into a stalled cross-functional effort and get it moving again. You will see everything the CEO sees, and you will be expected to form independent views and argue for them.

This role suits an experienced operator who has already provided leverage to senior executives and now wants a true seat at the table at a fast-growing fintech. For the right person, it is a launchpad into an executive leadership role at Coast.

What You'll Do

Act as a proxy for the CEO

- Represent the CEO in internal meetings, decisions, and escalations when he cannot be present, exercising judgment about what to resolve directly and what to bring back to him.

- Carry the CEO's agenda into the executive team: communicate his priorities and decisions clearly, and hold leaders accountable for commitments on his behalf.

- Serve as a trusted sounding board and thought partner, giving the CEO candid, well-reasoned counsel, including when your view differs from his.

Run the company's operating rhythm

- Own the leadership team's operating cadence: executive meetings, planning cycles, goal setting, and business reviews, ensuring each produces decisions and follow-through rather than discussion.

- Drive meeting preparation so the CEO walks in with the right context, agendas, and materials, and attendees leave aligned on outcomes.

- Track decisions and commitments across the executive team and project-manage them through to resolution so nothing falls through the cracks.

Own strategic special projects

- Take on complex, high-priority initiatives that don't yet have a clear owner, and drive them end to end: scope, plan, staff, execute, and land the result.

- Partner with the CEO and leadership team to develop, formalize, and implement strategies for company growth and operational improvement.

- Identify bottlenecks across the business, then troubleshoot and implement solutions with the relevant stakeholders, escalating to the CEO only when needed.

Support decision-making with research and analysis

- Conduct research and analysis on a wide range of topics, pulling the data and framing the trade-offs the CEO and leadership need to decide well.

- Prepare crisp, data-driven materials for the executive team, investors, and the board, and help manage board and investor communications.

What Success Looks Like

In your first year, you'll be successful if you:

- Operate as the CEO's genuine proxy: executives treat your direction as carrying his authority, and he trusts you to resolve issues in his absence without surprises.

- Have measurably improved how the executive team runs, with a reliable operating cadence and follow-through system so decisions consistently get executed.

- Have personally owned and delivered several company-critical projects that would not have happened, or would have moved far slower, without you.

- Are trusted across the leadership team as a fair, discreet, and effective partner who makes every executive around you more effective.

Requirements

- 7 to 12 years of experience, ideally combining a rigorous analytical foundation (management consulting, investment banking, strategy) with operating experience in a high-growth company; prior Chief of Staff, business operations leadership, or GM experience strongly preferred.

- A track record of earning the trust of CEOs or C-level executives and credibly representing them to senior stakeholders.

- Executive presence and influence: you can hold your own with, and when necessary push back on, experienced VPs and C-level leaders.

- Exceptional judgment and discretion; you handle confidential, sensitive, and politically delicate matters with ease.

- Strong analytical instincts: comfortable pulling metrics, spotting trends, and translating data into operational decisions.

- Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to align stakeholders at every level, from the board to the front line.

- AI-native mindset: you're already using AI tools to multiply your own output and you're excited to push further.

- Bias toward action and process-building; you don't wait for someone to hand you a playbook, and you can build structure in ambiguity without losing momentum.

- Experience in fintech, payments, B2B SaaS, or financial services preferred.

- New York City based; able to be in-office 3-4 days per week.

Compensation and Benefits

Our salary ranges are based on paying competitively for our size and industry, and are one part of our total compensation package that also includes benefits, signing bonus, and equity. Pay decisions are based on a number of factors, including scope and qualifications for the role, experience level, skillset, and balancing internal equity relative to other Coast employees. We expect the majority of candidates who are offered roles at Coast to fall healthily within the range based on these factors.

- Salary range: $175,000 to $225,000 annually

- Equity Grant: A meaningful ownership stake, weighted to reflect the seniority and impact of this role, with significant potential upside given Coast's early-stage trajectory

- Benefits Overview:

- Medical, dental and vision insurance

- Flexible paid time off (vacation, personal well being, paid holidays)

- Tools to help manage your financial wellness, including webinars, access to an equity tax advisory service, and company-sponsored 401(k)

- Paid parental leave

- $400 accessories allowance (a keyboard, mouse, headphones, etc.)

- Education stipend

- Free lunch every Friday

Coast is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We are building a diverse and inclusive environment, so we encourage people of all backgrounds to apply. We're an Equal Opportunity Employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, religion, disability, national origin, protected veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

jobs.title: Head of Partnerships
jobs.description:
What is Coast

Coast is re-imagining the trillion-dollar U.S. B2B card payments infrastructure, with a focus on the country's 500,000 commercial fleets, 40 million commercial vehicles, and many millions of commercial drivers. The incumbent technologies that cater to these customers are decades old, and businesses with fleets increasingly demand modern digital experiences and transparent financial services products. Coast's mission is to deliver this at a transformational scale, beginning with the Coast Fleet and Fuel Card built on a cutting-edge spend management platform.

About the Role

More and more of our best customers find us inside someone else's software. You'll own the function that makes that possible: Coast's Embedded and Channel Partnerships, one of the company's most important growth levers.

Coast is embedded natively in Samsara (NYSE: IOT). A fleet can sign up for Coast, set spend policies, and have transactions checked against live telematics data without leaving the Samsara platform. Samsara has called it their deepest fuel card integration yet , and it now sits at the center of the Fuel Command Center they launched in August. In July we shipped something similar with Fleetio, where fleet managers apply for and manage Coast cards inside Fleetio and every fuel and maintenance transaction posts automatically against the right vehicle. Underneath those two we have referral partners, resellers, and fleet management companies producing real volume, plus a pipeline of platform deals we haven't signed yet.

Customers who reach us this way close faster, cost far less to acquire, and tend to run bigger fleets.

We have the foundation of a channel that's poised to grow. Building one is the job: a second engine of growth alongside direct sales, reaching installed bases we could never call on ourselves.

You'll own it. That means sourcing and negotiating the next round of platform-scale distribution deals, activating the partnerships we already have so partner reps actually sell, and building a repeatable channel sales motion together with our Sales leadership. You'll lead a small team and continue to define the strategy and the playbook as we scale.

You'll report to Daniel Simon, our Founder and CEO.

What You'll Do

Own the channel as a business

- Own partner-sourced growth: pipeline, activated vehicles, revenue, and the CAC and payback numbers that determine whether the channel is worth running.

- Decide which categories of partner deserve our investment, across telematics and fleet management platforms, vertical and field service software, fleet management companies, resellers, associations and referral networks.

- Own the commercial model: revenue share, referral fees, minimum commitments, incentive structures, and the analysis that tells us what a partnership is worth before we sign it.

- Work out how Coast should be priced and packaged when it's sold inside someone else's product.

Strategize, source and close deals

- Own the full lifecycle of our partnerships: identifying and originating opportunities, and leading each one from the first conversation through to a signed agreement.

- Build relationships and presentations at the executive level.

- Partner closely with legal and finance to negotiate the terms that determine a deal's real value: exclusivity, term and termination, data rights, co-branding, service levels, and the marketing and sales commitments that decide whether a deal produces anything.

- Collaborate with Product and Engineering to define what the integration should be.

Build the launch plan for new and expanded partnerships

- Build the launch plan: enablement, training, incentive design, co-marketing, in-product placement, and joint pipeline reviews. Signing is the easy part.

- Get partner sales teams fluent in Coast through on-site trainings, ride-alongs, SKO presence and field time, so their reps think of us in a live deal.

- Design the incentives that make selling Coast worth a partner rep's time, and test them before scaling them.

- Own the in-product activation funnel with Product and Marketing: how a partner's customer discovers Coast, applies, and starts spending.

- Put governance in place that holds up. Executive sponsors on both sides, a QBR cadence, shared KPIs, and an escalation path people use.

Build the channel sales motion with Sales

- Work with Sales leadership on how partner-sourced demand gets routed, worked and compensated, including how Coast AEs and partner reps co-sell without colliding.

- Build the plumbing with RevOps and Marketing: attribution, deal registration, referral submission, forecasting and reporting we can run the business on.

- Write down what works. Onboarding, enablement, co-sell, co-marketing, QBRs, tiering, and a clear process for fixing or ending the partnerships that don't produce.

Lead and grow the internal partnerships team

- Hire, develop and lead the partnerships organization as the channel scales.

- Represent the channel to the executive team and the board, with a point of view and honest numbers.

What Success Looks Like

By 90 days

- You've mapped the partner landscape and have a prioritized view of where the next order of magnitude of channel volume comes from.

- You know our existing partnerships in depth: the people, the incentives, the integration, the deal terms, and why each one is or isn't producing.

- You can run a Coast demo and pitch the partner value proposition to a partner's CRO without help.

- One existing partnership is measurably more productive than when you arrived, and you can say exactly what you changed.

By 6 months

- Partner-sourced pipeline is growing, with leading indicators we track and trust: active partners, trained partner reps, registered deals, partner-sourced opportunities.

- You've signed a significant new distribution partnership, or materially expanded an existing one, on terms you negotiated.

- An activation playbook exists and has been run more than once, so a new partnership has a known path from signature to revenue.

- Partner-sourced deals get routed, worked and attributed cleanly, and Sales treats the channel as help.

By 12 months

- The channel is a meaningful and growing share of new customer acquisition, at lower CAC and faster payback than direct.

- Several partnerships are producing at scale, so the channel isn't riding on one relationship.

- The motion runs on infrastructure and playbooks that keep working while you're on vacation.

- When the next platform in this market decides to embed payments, we get the call.

Requirements

- 10+ years in business development, embedded partnerships, or channel sales, ideally with at least one stretch where you owned distribution as a business: a number, unit economics you answered for, and real influence over product, pricing, and packaging.

- You've sourced, negotiated, and closed a large embedded or distribution partnership yourself: an integration, a revenue share, joint GTM commitments, and a long negotiation with a counterparty much bigger than you.

- You think in installed bases: how many of a partner's customers are reachable, through what surface, at what conversion, and what would move that number.

- Experienced at hiring and leading a partnerships team.

- You've worked alongside a direct sales organization and know how to keep a channel from turning into a fight over credit.

- Strong analytical instincts: comfortable pulling metrics, spotting trends, and translating data into operational decisions

- Strong relationship builder with excellent communication and presentation skills.

- AI-native mindset: you're already using AI tools in your daily work and you're excited to push further

- High ownership mindset: you proactively identify opportunities and drive them

- Organized and process-driven; able to manage multiple partners and workstreams with clarity.

- Ability to thrive in ambiguity and build structure to scale the function.

- Experience in fintech, payments, B2B SaaS, or financial services preferred

- Willingness to travel approximately 20% for partner meetings and tradeshows

- New York City based; able to be in-office 3–4 days per week

Compensation and Benefits

Our salary ranges are based on paying competitively for our size and industry, and are one part of our total compensation package that also includes benefits and equity. Pay decisions are based on a number of factors, including scope and qualifications for the role, experience level, skillset, and balancing internal equity relative to other Coast employees. We expect the majority of candidates who are offered roles at Coast to fall healthily within the range based on these factors.

Salary range: $190,000 – $250,000 annually, plus a performance based bonus opportunity depending on level determined during the interview process

Equity Grant: Meaningful potential upside given Coast's early-stage trajectory

Benefits Overview:

jobs.title: Lifecycle Marketing Manager
jobs.description:
What is Coast

Coast is re-imagining the trillion-dollar U.S. B2B card payments infrastructure, with a focus on the country's 500,000 commercial fleets, 40 million commercial vehicles, and many millions of commercial drivers. The incumbent technologies that cater to these customers are decades old, and businesses with fleets increasingly demand modern digital experiences and transparent financial services products. Coast's mission is to deliver this at a transformational scale, beginning with the Coast Fleet and Fuel Card built on a cutting-edge spend management platform.

About the Role

We're looking for a Lifecycle Marketing Manager to own how Coast activates, retains, and grows every customer after they sign. Our fuel card is the first product customers get from Coast and our lifecycle marketing motion is how we turn this wedge into a lasting, multi-product relationship—moving a business that only uses Coast for fuel spending into a customer that lives their entire financial life through Coast. This expansion is key to Coast and it happens through the programs you'll build.

You'll develop deep expertise on our customers, our products, and the moments that matter across their journey. With that knowledge you will build, run, and own the automated programs that carry them from first touch to an activated, engaged, expanding customer. This is a full-funnel lifecycle across our owned channels and covers everything from lead nurture, onboarding, activation, cross-sell, retention, and winback.

This is a hands-on role with real ownership. You'll be making strategic choices yourself and building journeys in Braze as you write our lifecycle playbook in real time.

What You'll Do

- Own full-funnel lifecycle journeys end-to-end

- Build and run nurture, onboarding, activation, engagement, retention, and winback programs in Braze across email, in-app, push, and SMS

- Use behavioral and product data to trigger the right message, at the right moment, for the right persona

- Drive fuel → non-fuel expansion through owned channels

- Own the lifecycle motion that moves fuel customers onto corporate cards, Bill Pay, and more — Coast's single biggest growth lever

- Partner with Product Marketing and Growth teams on the narrative, offers, and timing that get customers to adopt more

- Turn new signups into activated, transacting customers

- Design onboarding journeys that get a new fleet issuing cards, setting controls, and transacting fast

- Identify drop-off points and partner with Product, Sales, and Customer Success to close them

- Partner cross-functionally to build the system

- Work with Growth Engineering on the data, events, and integrations that power triggered journeys

- Work with Revenue Operations, Sales, and CS to time lifecycle touches around the sales cycle and each customer's real activity

- Own measurement and experimentation

- Own the metrics for every program — deliverability, engagement, activation rate, attach rate, retention

- Run a real testing cadence, report what's working, kill what isn't, and use results to influence our overall GTM motion

What Success Looks Like

In your first year, you'll be successful if you:

- Ship a reliable full-funnel lifecycle program in Braze — onboarding, activation, expansion, retention, winback — that beats the baseline it replaces

- Lift new-customer activation rate and shorten time to first transaction

- Grow non-fuel attach (corporate card and Bill Pay) across the fuel base through owned-channel journeys

- Reduce churn with early-warning triggers and re-engagement that measurably keep more customers

- Recover a meaningful share of abandoned credit applications and accelerate growth of qualified opportunities with nurture journeys

Requirements

- 4+ years in lifecycle, CRM, product marketing, or marketing ops/analytics

- Hands-on mastery of a modern lifecycle platform; direct Braze experience is a strong plus

- AI-native mindset: you're already using AI tools in your daily work and you're excited to push further

- Strong analytical instincts: comfortable pulling and interpreting metrics yourself, designing clean A/B tests, and translating data into decisions

- Excellent written and verbal communication, including strong copy instincts (you can write a subject line and a lifecycle email that drive action)

- Bias to action, strong agency, comfort with ambiguity, and propensity for first principles systems thinking: you don't wait for someone to hand you a playbook

- Experience in B2B fintech, payments, financial services, or SaaS strongly preferred

- Salt Lake City or New York City based - we are in office 3+ days/week

jobs.title: Manager of Customer Success
jobs.description:
Coast is re-imagining the trillion-dollar U.S. B2B card payments infrastructure, with a focus on the country’s 500,000 commercial fleets, 40 million commercial vehicles, and many million commercial drivers. The incumbent technologies that cater to these customers are decades old, and drivers and fleets increasingly demand modern digital experiences and affordable and transparent financial services products. Coast's mission is to deliver them at a transformational scale, beginning with the Coast Fleet and Fuel Card built on a cutting-edge spend management platform.

About the Role

We’re looking for a hands on, people-first Manager of Customer Success to lead our frontline CSMs while owning a book of business. This player-coach model is core to how Coast builds empathy, credibility, and process excellence across our customer lifecycle. You’ll mentor, hire, and develop a team responsible for delivering exceptional onboarding, activation, and retention outcomes for all of our customer segments.

What Success Looks Like

- Deliver consistent customer value across the lifecycle

- Deliver excellent GRR & NRR—and raise it further through proactive health monitoring and disciplined retention and expansion execution.

- Increase onboarding velocity and fleet activation so customers hit time-to-value faster and ramp usage more consistently.

- Be a true player-coach: excited to own accounts, demonstrate product + CS fluency, and raise team performance via a standardized 1:1 coaching framework.

- Enhance expansion pipeline by consistently identifying, creating, and progressing CSQOs into qualified expansion opportunities.

What You’ll Do

- Lead & Coach: Manage and mentor a team of high-performing CSMs, focusing on call coaching, onboarding execution, fleet activation, and account health.

- Own Accounts: Carry a book of business to stay close to the customer experience and model best-in-class onboarding, retention, and expansion skills.

- Drive Activation: Ensure your team drives velocity and depth of onboarding.

- Create Value: Help CSMs demonstrate customer value across the lifecycle—from onboarding through maturity—with account-specific plans tied to clear use cases.

- Maximize Expansion: Support CSMs in creating CSQOs and building a proactive expansion pipeline.

- Upskill the Team: Develop a repeatable 1:1 coaching and enablement framework to improve onboarding, account health, and teammate performance.

- Build Systems Excellence: Champion operational rigor and data fluency across Salesforce, Sigma, Outreach, and our AI toolkit to guide prioritization and performance.

What We're Looking For

- 5+ years in Customer Success or Account Management, with 2+ years managing CSMs or frontline customer-facing teams

- A proven player-coach: you lead by example while enabling others to succeed

- Track record of high-touch onboarding and expansion motions in SMB and mid-market

- Expertise in creating structure from ambiguity—using data, systems, and coaching to drive repeatable outcomes

- Strong communicator with a bias for clarity, urgency, and action

- Deep empathy for customers—and for the CSMs who serve them

- Bonus: familiarity with fintech, SaaS, or operations-heavy customer segments

Compensation

Our salary ranges are based on paying competitively for our size and industry, and are one part of our total compensation package that also includes benefits, signing bonus, and equity. Pay decisions are based on a number of factors, including scope and qualifications for the role, experience level, skillset, and balancing internal equity relative to other Coast employees. We expect the majority of the candidates who are offered roles at Coast to fall healthily within the range based on these factors.

- On Target Earnings: $120,000 - $140,000

- Equity grant: commensurate with level determined at the discretion of the company, with meaningful potential upside given the company’s early stage

- Benefits overview:

- Medical, dental and vision insurance

- Unlimited paid time off (vacation, personal well being, paid holidays)

- Paid parental leave

- $400 accessories allowance for home office setup to be spent on a keyboard, mouse, headphones, etc.

- Free lunch every Friday

About Coast

Coast is founded and led by Daniel Simon, who previously cofounded Bread (breadpayments.com), a leading payments and credit technology firm backed by some of the world’s top VCs which was acquired for $500MM+ in 2020.

Coast has raised $165M in total funding — our recent $40M Series B equity round was led by ICONIQ Growth with participation from Thomvest, and Synchrony. We're also backed by top fintech and mobility venture funds – including Accel, Insight Partners, Better Tomorrow Ventures, Avid Ventures, Bessemer Venture Partners, BoxGroup, Foundation Capital, Greycroft, Colle – and premier angel investors – including Max Levchin (Affirm), Josh Abramowitz (Bread), Jason Gardner (Marqeta), William Hockey (Plaid), Ryan Petersen (Flexport), and many others.

jobs.title: VP, People
jobs.description:
What is Coast

Coast is re-imagining the trillion-dollar U.S. B2B card payments infrastructure, with a focus on the country's 500,000 commercial fleets, 40 million commercial vehicles, and many millions of commercial drivers. Our customers include plumbing and HVAC contractors, trucking companies, and last-mile delivery businesses. The incumbent technologies that cater to these customers are decades old, and businesses with fleets increasingly demand modern digital experiences and transparent financial services products. Coast's mission is to deliver this at scale, beginning with the Coast Fleet and Fuel Card, built on Coast's spend management platform.

Coast has invested heavily in building a culture of humble, collaborative, talented, and hardworking people, across every function and level of seniority, who believe in the company's mission and enjoy working with one another. That culture has been the foundation of Coast's success so far - see our Glassdoor - and protecting it through the next stage of growth, as Coast adds new functions and new leaders, is a central part of this role.

About the Role

Coast hired its first people operations lead two years ago to stand up the basics: benefits, onboarding, policies, and the day-to-day experience of the Coast offices. Since then, Coast has grown its total funding to $135 million and its team to about 130 people across two offices: our New York City headquarters, home to roughly two thirds of the team, and our sales and operations office in Utah. The People function now needs to grow with the company.

You'll be Coast's first VP, People, the company's senior people leader, building and running the function end to end: People Operations, Total Rewards, Talent (recruiting, performance, and career development), and Culture. You'll partner directly with the executive team on org design, leadership development, and the people decisions that shape how Coast scales, while making sure the fundamentals (comp, performance, compliance, onboarding) are run well.

This is a build role: you'll inherit a foundation and turn it into a people strategy that keeps pace with the business. You'll report to Stephen Rosen , Coast's SVP of Operations, and lead a team that includes our Head of Talent, People Ops Lead and a growing people team.

What You'll Do

Build and lead the People function

- Take People Operations from a foundational function to a full People org: design the team, the roadmap, and the systems (HRIS, payroll, benefits administration) that scale with headcount.

- Own the People budget and the tooling decisions that come with it.

- Hire, develop, and lead the People team as it grows.

Partner with the executive team and managers

- Work with leadership and the CEO on organizational design, headcount planning, and the People implications of major business decisions.

- Coach managers through hiring, performance, promotions, and difficult conversations, and build the manager enablement program Coast doesn't have yet.

- Be the person leaders and teammates trust with hard people problems.

Own recruiting, performance, and career development

- Design and run the performance review and promotion cycles, and the career frameworks that make "what good looks like" clear at every level.

- Build the systems that catch performance and engagement issues early, while there is still time to address them.

- Lead recruiting through our Head of Talent, owning hiring plans, process, and the candidate experience for both offices, including sales and operations hiring in Utah.

- Partner with hiring managers to keep the hiring bar high as Coast grows.

Drive compensation, equity, and benefits strategy

- Design Coast's compensation philosophy and pay bands, and partner with Finance on the equity strategy that keeps offers competitive.

- Source and manage the benefits, perks, and platforms that make Coast a place people want to build their careers.

- Run comp cycles with the rigor and fairness a growing company needs.

- Partner with Finance, Sales, and Revenue Operations leadership on sales compensation plans for account executives, BDRs, and other commissioned roles.

Shape culture, engagement, and employee experience

- Keep Coast's culture intact as headcount grows past the size where culture happens by accident.

- Lead team events, office experience, and company traditions in both New York and Utah, so the Utah team has the same access to leadership, information, and career paths as the headquarters team.

- Run engagement surveys and other feedback loops, and turn what you hear into action.

Own compliance and risk

- Make sure Coast's policies, records, and practices comply with employment law in New York, Utah, and anywhere else Coast employs people.

- Build the HR infrastructure (records, policies, and processes) that holds up under scrutiny as Coast scales and potentially expands into new states or geographies.

- Own worker classification and wage-and-hour compliance, including timekeeping and overtime for salaried non-exempt roles such as customer service representatives and BDRs, and written commission agreements for commissioned sales roles.

What Success Looks Like

By 90 days

- You've met every person at Coast, including time on the ground with the Utah team, and you have a clear read on where the People function is strong and where it's thin.

- Your review of the current comp, benefits, and performance processes has produced a prioritized plan to fix what's broken.

- Managers know who you are and have brought you at least one real problem.

- You and leadership have agreed on the three People priorities that matter most this year.

By 6 months

- Coast has a documented compensation philosophy and pay bands, and hiring managers use them.

- At least one performance review cycle has run under your design, and managers and employees trust the process.

- The People team, including recruiting, has clear ownership of onboarding, benefits, hiring, and employee support, and a plan for the roles it needs next.

- Coast's HR policies and records are compliant and audit-ready across every state and location Coast operates in.

By 12 months

- Coast's people strategy is a direct input to the company's growth and headcount plans.

- Engagement and retention are measurably better, and you can point to what you changed.

- The People function runs on infrastructure and playbooks, and the team handles day-to-day issues without you in the room.

- Leaders in both New York and Utah bring the People team into major decisions early.

Requirements

- 10+ years in People/HR roles, including experience leading a People function at a high-growth startup that has successfully scaled beyond Coast's current stage of maturity.

- Track record designing compensation philosophy, pay bands, and equity strategy, and running comp cycles that scale with headcount.

- Experience coaching managers through performance, promotion, and org design decisions, and building manager enablement programs where none existed.

- Recruiting leadership: you've managed a recruiting team and built hiring processes that hold the bar as hiring volume grows.

- Deep knowledge of employment law and HR compliance across multiple U.S. states, including New York.

- Experience supporting a multi-site workforce that includes non-exempt and commissioned sales and operations teams based outside headquarters, including sales compensation design.

- Comfortable operating at the executive table: strong judgment, discretion, and the ability to influence without formal authority.

- Strong analytical instincts: comfortable working in HRIS and comp data and turning it into a recommendation.

- High ownership mindset: when a process doesn't exist yet, you build it.

- Experience in fintech, payments, or B2B SaaS preferred.

- New York City based; able to be in-office 3–4 days per week and to travel to our Utah office at least once a quarter.

Compensation and Benefits

Our salary ranges are based on paying competitively for our size and industry, and are one part of our total compensation package that also includes benefits and equity. Pay decisions are based on a number of factors, including scope and qualifications for the role, experience level, skillset, and balancing internal equity relative to other Coast employees. We expect the majority of candidates who are offered roles at Coast to fall within the range based on these factors.

Salary range: $250,000 – $280,000

Equity Grant: Meaningful potential upside given Coast's stage and growth

Benefits Overview:

- Medical, dental, and vision insurance

- Flexible paid time off (vacation, personal well-being, paid holidays)

- Tools to help manage your financial wellness, including webinars, access to an equity tax advisory service, and company-sponsored 401(k)

- Paid parental leave

- $400 accessories allowance (a keyboard, mouse, headphones, etc.)

- Education stipend

- Free lunch every Friday

Coast is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We are building a diverse and inclusive environment, so we encourage people of all backgrounds to apply. jobs.title: Compliance Analyst
jobs.description:
What is Coast

Coast is re-imagining the trillion-dollar U.S. B2B card payments infrastructure, with a focus on the country’s 500,000 commercial fleets, 40 million commercial vehicles, and many millions of commercial drivers. The incumbent technologies that cater to these customers are decades old, and businesses with fleets increasingly demand modern digital experiences and transparent financial services products. Coast’s mission is to deliver this at a transformational scale, beginning with the Coast Fleet and Fuel Card built on a cutting-edge spend management platform.

About the Role

We're hiring a Compliance Analyst to help build and run our BSA/AML/OFAC program. This is a hands-on role for someone who wants to work close to the transaction data  investigating alerts, spotting patterns, and turning findings into action while helping shape how a compliance program gets built from the ground up at a fast-moving fintech. You'll work directly with senior compliance leadership, giving you visibility and influence well beyond a typical analyst seat.

This role is a strong fit for someone who wants ownership early in their career: you'll help define the processes, not just follow them, and you'll have room to bring AI-powered tools into how the work gets done from day one.

What You’ll Do

- Monitor and investigate suspicious activity

- Conduct account and transaction-level reviews to identify unusual patterns and escalate suspicious activity.

- Review system-generated alerts and support the drafting of Unusual Activity Reports (UARs).

- Support the sanctions and AML program

- Apply OFAC screening and BSA/AML controls to daily case work and escalations.

- Identify and label patterns of unusual activity, including reporting to financial partners.

- Track developments in BSA, AML and OFAC enforcement and guidance, and flag implications for Coast's practices.

- Track KRIs/KPIs that measure the health of the AML program.

- Respond to audit, partner bank, and regulatory requests.

- Use SQL and internal/external data sources to spot system vulnerabilities and compliance gaps.

- Testing and oversight

- Conduct quality assurance testing of underwriting and credit decisioning processes, adverse action notices, and account practices for ECOA, SCRA, and FCRA adherence, collaborating with process owners to build corrective action plans where gaps are identified.

- Other compliance support

- Support additional compliance initiatives and cross-functional projects as they arise, including emerging regulatory requirements and policy development.

- Assist with ad hoc risk assessments and internal audits as needed.

- Help build out processes and documentation for new or evolving compliance areas where none yet exist.

- Respond to compliance-related questions from internal teams (product, engineering, sales, customer support) and escalate as appropriate.

- Take on other compliance-related projects and duties to support important Company initiatives and priorities.

- Partner across the business

- Work cross-functionally with Legal, Risk, and Product to keep policies and controls current.

- Support senior Compliance team members on key initiatives and reporting to governance committees.

What Success Looks Like

In your first year, you'll be successful if you:

- Independently manage a caseload of BSA/AML/OFAC alerts and investigations, from initial review through UAR filing.

- Become the go-to point of contact for day-to-day BSA/AML/OFAC compliance operations.

- Identify and help close at least one meaningful gap in monitoring coverage or process.

- Build a trusted, responsive working relationship with our partner bank and stakeholders.

- Bring AI tools into your workflow in a way that measurably speeds up investigations or reporting.

- Contribute analysis or reporting that shapes a real decision made by compliance leadership.

- Demonstrate you can flex into adjacent compliance work as needed, not just your core caseload.

Requirements

- 2+ years of experience in a BSA/AML/OFAC compliance role, ideally at a fintech or other closely regulated industry.

- AI-native mindset : you're already using AI tools in your daily work and you're excited to push further.

- Experience with transaction monitoring or alerts screening systems, and comfort writing SQL queries against large datasets.

- Strong analytical instincts  comfortable pulling metrics, spotting trends, and translating data into operational decisions.

- Excellent written and verbal communication.

- Bias toward action and process-building  you don't wait for someone to hand you a playbook.

- Comfortable in ambiguity you can build structure where none exists without losing momentum.

- Experience in fintech, payments, B2B SaaS, or financial services preferred.

- Based in Salt Lake City or New York City; able to be in-office 3–4 days per week.

Compensation and Benefits

Our salary ranges are based on paying competitively for our size and industry, and are one part of our total compensation package that also includes benefits and equity. Pay decisions are based on a number of factors, including scope and qualifications for the role, experience level, skillset, and balancing internal equity relative to other Coast employees. We expect the majority of candidates who are offered roles at Coast to fall healthily within the range based on these factors.

Salary range : $60,000 – $75,000 annually

Equity Grant : Meaningful potential upside given Coast’s early-stage trajectory

Benefits Overview :

- Medical, dental and vision insurance

- Flexible paid time off (vacation, personal well being, paid holidays)

- Tools to help manage your financial wellness, including webinars, access to an equity tax advisory service, and company-sponsored 401(k)

- Paid parental leave

- $400 accessories allowance (a keyboard, mouse, headphones, etc.)

- Education stipend

- Free lunch every Friday

Coast is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We are building a diverse and inclusive environment, so we encourage people of all backgrounds to apply. We’re an Equal Opportunity Employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, religion, disability, national origin, protected veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

Check out the latest podcast interview on Fintech Layer Cake with Coast Founder Daniel Simon !
